name: AI Agent Kill Switch
description: Stop one compromised AI agent: block its gateway key, deactivate the provider key behind it, kill the agent process on the host, and ask the model one bounded question about whether the account itself needs demoting. Every containment step is behind an approval, and the approval declares what happens if nobody answers. Distinct from services/actions kill_switch.py, which is the platform-wide autonomy stop and is not an agent control.
author: AiSOC

gateway_key.description: Virtual key the agent presents at the AI gateway

provider_key_id.description: Provider API key id behind the agent

principal.description: Person or service identity the agent acts for

steps.name: Read the gateway key's current state
Is this the agent's own scheduled work or somebody else driving it?

params.question: Given the evidence, does this activity look like the agent's own scheduled work, or like a third party driving the agent's credentials?

params.reason: Blocking the gateway key and deactivating the provider key stops every workload using this agent's credentials, not only the compromised one.

steps.name: Kill the agent process on the host
Tell the agent's owner what was stopped and why

params.message: An AI agent acting for you was contained: its gateway key was blocked and its process stopped. The provider key behind it needs a separate decision.
